title: The pulse and downstrokes
summary: Strum down on every beat and switch between E minor and A minor without losing the pulse.

steps.title: Meet E minor
steps.text: Two fingers, and all six strings ring. Watch where each finger goes, then copy the shape.

steps.title: Meet A minor
steps.text: Am is the Em shape moved one string toward the floor, plus your index finger. Skip the thickest string.

steps.title: Strum on the beat
steps.text: One downstroke on each click: 1, 2, 3, 4. Your hand still comes back up between beats; it just misses the strings.

steps.title: Play along
steps.text: Two bars of Em, two bars of Am. If a change is late, keep strumming anyway: the pulse matters more than a perfect chord.

steps.title: Check yourself
steps.goal: 4 bars at 70 bpm without losing the pulse

title: Down-up eighth notes
summary: Add upstrokes between the beats for a steady down-up motion.

steps.title: Down on the number, up on the "and"
steps.text: Count "1 and 2 and 3 and 4 and". Down on the numbers, up on every "and". Upstrokes are lighter and mostly catch the thin strings.

steps.title: Play along
steps.text: Keep your wrist loose and the motion even, like shaking water off your hand.

title: The folk pattern
summary: Learn ↓ ↓↑ ↑↓↑, the pattern behind countless acoustic pop songs.

steps.title: Meet G major
steps.text: Three fingers spread across the neck. All six strings ring.

steps.title: Meet D major
steps.text: A small triangle on the thin strings. Start your strum on the 4th string.
Your hand never stops: down-up on every beat. On the "and" of 1 and on beat 3 it moves without touching the strings.

steps.title: Play along
steps.text: Say it out loud: "down, down-up, up-down-up". Start slow; the speed comes on its own.

steps.title: Check yourself
steps.goal: 8 bars of the folk pattern without stopping

title: Accents and muted strums
summary: Make the beat groove: hit 2 and 4 harder, then turn them into a percussive "chuck".

steps.title: Meet C major
steps.text: Three fingers in a diagonal line. Skip the thickest string: start your strum on the 5th string.

steps.title: Accents on 2 and 4
steps.text: The same down-up motion, but beats 2 and 4 (marked >) are louder. That's where the snare drum lands in most pop songs.

steps.title: The chuck
steps.text: On beats 2 and 4, let the side of your strumming hand land on the strings as you strum down. The strings go dead and you get a short "chk" instead of a chord. Lift the palm right away so the next strum rings.

steps.title: Play along
steps.text: Strum, chk, strum-strum, chk. If the chuck rings like a chord, press your palm down a bit more. If the next strum sounds dead, lift sooner.

steps.title: Check yourself
steps.goal: 8 bars with the chuck on 2 and 4 at 80 bpm

title: Anchor fingers and guide fingers
summary: Change chords faster by moving fewer fingers: keep anchors down and land shapes as one.

steps.title: C → Am: two anchors
steps.text: Fingers 1 and 2 don't move at all, so keep them pressed. Only your ring finger travels.

steps.title: G → D: move the shape
steps.text: No finger can stay here. Lift all three together, make the D shape in the air on the way, and land them at the same time.

steps.title: C ↔ Am
steps.text: One change every bar. Watch your anchors: they should never leave the strings.

steps.title: All four chords
steps.text: G, D, C, Am, one bar each. Land each shape as a group, even if a string buzzes at first. Then open the Trainer tab and aim for 30 clean changes in 60 seconds.

steps.title: Check yourself
steps.goal: 8 bars with a clean change every bar at 60 bpm

title: Change on the last beat
summary: Land every new chord right on beat 1 by leaving the old one a little early.

steps.title: Leave early
steps.text: The "Next" sign turns orange on beat 4. That's your cue: on the last upstroke, lift your fingers and strum the open strings while they travel. Nobody hears it, and you land on beat 1 on time.

steps.title: G → C
steps.text: Every finger moves, so this is the hardest change in the lesson. Lead with your ring finger and let the others follow.

steps.title: D → Em
steps.text: Em only needs two fingers, so it's an easy landing. Aim for the 5th and 4th strings and strum all six.

steps.title: Play along
steps.text: One chord per bar. Your strumming hand is the clock: it keeps moving no matter what the other hand is doing.

steps.title: Check yourself
steps.goal: Every change on time for 8 bars at 70 bpm

title: Seventh chords and the blues
summary: Learn E7, A7, D7 and B7, then play a full 12-bar blues in E.

steps.title: Meet E7
steps.text: E7 is E major with one finger lifted. Two fingers, all six strings ring, and the open 4th string adds the bluesy 7th.

steps.title: Meet A7
steps.text: Two fingers on the 2nd fret with the 3rd string left open between them. Skip the thickest string.

steps.title: Meet D7
steps.text: An upside-down triangle on the thin strings. Start your strum on the 4th string.

steps.title: Meet B7
steps.text: Your first four-finger chord. Build it from the middle finger out, and skip the 6th string.

steps.title: B7 → E7: a pivot
steps.text: Finger 2 sits on the same spot in both chords. Keep it down and use it as a pivot.

steps.title: 12-bar blues in E
steps.text: This progression is behind thousands of songs: 4 bars of E7, 2 of A7, 2 of E7, then one bar each of B7, A7, E7 and B7, which turns you back to the start.

steps.title: Check yourself
steps.goal: A full 12-bar blues in E at 70 bpm

title: Closing song: the I–V–vi–IV progression
summary: Play a whole song with the four most common chords in pop: G, D, Em and C.

steps.title: The four chords of pop
steps.text: G, D, Em, C, in that order, is the I–V–vi–IV progression. You'll hear it in pop songs from every decade, and you already know all four chords.

steps.title: Em → C
steps.text: The change from Em to C is the one that usually trips people up here. Watch it a few times before you play.

steps.title: The verse
steps.text: One bar each. Start at Medium; when it feels easy, switch to Normal.

steps.title: The whole song
steps.text: The verse twice, then a chorus that starts on C and lands on G. Follow the big chord name and the "Next" sign.

steps.title: Check yourself
steps.goal: The whole song, 16 bars, at 90 bpm

title: Arpeggios with a pick
summary: Hold the chord and pick the strings one at a time, letting every note ring.

steps.title: One string at a time
steps.text: Pick the bass note on beat 1, then strings 3, 2, 1, 2, 3, 2, 1. The numbers are string numbers: 1 is the thinnest. On C, the bass note is the 5th string.

steps.title: The bass note moves
steps.text: On G the bass note is the 6th string. The rest of the pattern stays the same, so only the first note needs aiming.

steps.title: Play along
steps.text: Let every note ring into the next. If a note sounds dead, a finger is touching that string: arch your fingers more and press with the tips.

steps.title: Check yourself
steps.goal: 8 bars of clean arpeggios, no dead strings

title: F with a partial barre
summary: Get the F chord to ring on four strings, with an easy version to start.

steps.title: The easy F first
steps.text: Fmaj7 sounds close to F and needs no barre. Use it in songs while the real F gets stronger.

steps.title: F with a small barre
steps.text: Lay your index finger flat across the two thinnest strings at fret 1. Roll it slightly onto its bony side so both strings ring.

steps.title: C → F
steps.text: Your index finger stays on the 2nd string and flattens over the 1st. Middle and ring fingers each move one string toward the thin strings.

steps.title: C → F → C → G
steps.text: Strum only the 4 thin strings on F. If a string buzzes, press closer to the fret wire, not harder.

steps.title: Check yourself
steps.goal: F rings on all 4 strings in time, twice through

title: Alternating bass (basic Carter style)
summary: Pick a bass note, strum, pick another bass note, strum: the classic "boom-chick".

steps.title: Boom-chick on C
steps.text: Bass note on beat 1, a light strum on 2, the other bass note on 3, strum on 4. On C the bass goes from the 5th string to the 4th.

steps.title: Boom-chick on G
steps.text: On G the bass jumps from the 6th string to the 4th. Your pick has to find the string without looking, so go slowly at first.

steps.title: Play along
steps.text: Keep the bass notes strong and the strums light. That contrast is what makes the style.

steps.title: Check yourself
steps.goal: Bass and strum together for 8 bars at 70 bpm

title: Closing song: vi–IV–I–V with arpeggios
summary: Put it all together: Am, F, C and G as a fingerpicked-style song with a pick.

steps.title: Am → F
steps.text: Your index finger stays on the 2nd string and flattens over the 1st. Middle and ring fingers cross over to their new strings.

steps.title: The arpeggio again
steps.text: Same pattern as Lesson 9. On F the bass note is the 4th string, because the two thickest strings stay silent.

steps.title: The verse
steps.text: If F isn't ringing yet, play Fmaj7 instead, but keep the arpeggio going: never stop the right hand.

steps.title: The whole song
steps.text: The verse twice, then a chorus that turns it around: F, G, C, Am. End on a long C and let it ring.

steps.title: Check yourself
steps.goal: The whole song with arpeggios, 16 bars at 70 bpm
